title: Sweep stamps attempt-log `at` as empty string in production
evidence:
sweep.gleam:164: `  Ok(run(db_conn, deps, "", sentry, default_batch_limit))`
sweep_handler.gleam:39: `          now_iso: "",`
sweep.gleam:705: `    #("at", json.string(at)),`
sweep.gleam:715: `    #("at", json.string(at)),`
sweep.gleam:533: `        at: now_iso,`
messages.gleam:426: `  <> email_client.escape_html(entry.at)`
messages.gleam:30: `// ([{at, channel, outcome, detail}]; the sweep stamps `at` when it builds`
detail: Every sweep-appended attempt entry is stamped with now_iso, hardcoded "" in both production entry points. The warm-handoff email renders entry.at verbatim, so landlords see blank timestamps (": email, delivered") and terminal result attempts carry "" for RC4.
recommended_fix: Pass a real ISO-8601 now (e.g. gleam_time now, formatted) from bootstrap and sweep_handler instead of "", or resolve "" to the current time inside outcome_entry/skipped_entry.

title: Warm-handoff notification loss on dispatch error is unrecoverable
detail: The guarded advance to attempt_count=4 commits before dispatch; if the in-app notification insert fails (DB error, logged only as a warning), the §8.3 unreachable notification is lost forever — the T+144 terminal is silent by design and no later tick re-dispatches.
recommended_fix: When notify_reference_unreachable returns Error, capture a Sentry event (and consider re-dispatching at the T+144 terminal when the notification row is absent).

title: Persistent T0 claim failure re-sends the invite every 15 minutes with no escalation
detail: Claim errors are all treated as transient; a persistent one (constraint violation, schema drift) leaves the row queued and due, so each 15-min tick re-mints a token and re-sends a full invite forever — no Sentry, no failed terminal, and the discarded entries under-count the sends.
recommended_fix: Escalate after repeated claim failures: track consecutive Errors per row (or match non-transient Postgres error codes) and mark_failed + Sentry instead of re-sending.
